text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: high restart rate detected in cluster/us-west-2/serving-pool (node-group: gpu-standard). Severity: P1. Symptom: repeated container restarts with CUDA errors and OOM during model warmup. Monitoring: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/serving-pool

Priya (oncall): @here I'm on it. seeing 5xx spike and node restarts. tagging eng-runtime and SRE. anyone oncall for runtime? :eyes:

Alex (runtime): I'm on. quick snapshot: lots of warmup failures while initializing models -> deserialization EOF + compile cache timeouts, then container restarts with `CUDA: driver lost` on some pods. example logs:
```
E 04/01 12:34:56 model_warmup: deserialize failed: EOF
E 04/01 12:34:56 compile_cache: compile timeout after 120000ms for kernel selection
E 04/01 12:34:57 runtime: cuda: driver lost (NVIDIA 525.78?)
panic: runtime error: device reset
... container restarted ...
```

Liam (eng-runtime): confirming. We're seeing a small subset of nodes (worker-2, worker-5) in a restart loop. Warmup appears to trigger heavy device memory pressure + a driver reset on those nodes. Not all models are affected; large models during eager prefill are the common factor.

Priya (oncall): priority actions?

Liam (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations I'd push now: 1) disable eager warmup for the impacted model(s) to avoid prefill during pod start, 2) increase compile timeout to reduce unnecessary compile aborts, 3) shift traffic to quantized fallback variant while we stabilize. I can push a config patch and a routing change.

Alex (runtime): I'll push a hotfix config to the serving configmap. patch snippet: 
```yaml
# temp mitigation - disable warmup and extend compile timeout
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  model.rdx-open-llama-7b-v2.warmup.enabled: "false"
  runtime.compile_timeout_ms: "300000"
```
Applying to us-west-2 serving pool now.

Priya (oncall): @Liam can you route 50% traffic to `rdx-open-llama-7b-v2-q` (quantized) in us-west-2? command we use: `rw route set --model rdx-open-llama-7b-v2-q --weight 50 --region us-west-2`

Liam (eng-runtime): running that now. updating rollout and will watch.

Rosa (Customer Ops): quick customer impact note: dashboards show ~12 customers saw elevated 5xx (mostly high concurrency) since 12:34 UTC. one customer (acme-pay) reported API errors. We should prepare a focused notification for customers above x qps.

Alex (runtime): status update: config applied to replica set, new pods come up without running warmup. observed a drop in restart counts on nodes which picked up new pods. older pods still in crash loop on worker-2. logs show kernel OOPS on that node: `kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:xx:xx): 79` — suggests a GPU driver fault on that host.

Mei (SRE Lead): cordon and drain worker-2, evict pods to other nodes, and escalate node to infra team for repro/driver logs. If we see more nodes with OOPS, prepare to scale down warmup cluster-wide.

Liam (eng-runtime): cordon/drain commands issued: `kubectl cordon worker-2 && kubectl drain worker-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — evict succeeded. New pods scheduled on healthy nodes.

Priya (oncall): routing shift now at 50%. monitoring shows request error-rate dropping from 18% -> 6% over last 5m, latency for routed requests stable. good.

Rosa (Customer Ops): preparing email note for affected customers. suggested text: short incident summary, mitigation in place, timeline, and point of contact. will send after you OK.

Alex (runtime): one more thing: we observed model deserialization errors in logs on restart: `deserialize: unexpected EOF` for one artifact blob — probably artifact streaming hit mid-transfer when pod crashed. We'll re-verify artifact integrity and retry warmup on a healthy node.

Liam (eng-runtime): also bumped compile_timeout to 300s in config; hoping to avoid spurious compile failures. There is a longer-term followup: review kernel/driver versions across cluster (some nodes on 525.x, others 522.x). SRE/Infra will reconcile.

Mei (SRE Lead): agreed. infra to collect `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi --query`, and driver package info from worker-2 and worker-5. schedule a post-incident triage. If root cause is driver regression, we'll coordinate node reimage/rollback.

Priya (oncall): customer impact recap for status page: "Partial serving degradation in us-west-2 between 12:34-13:05 UTC. Some requests returned 5xx or experienced higher latency. Majority traffic served by fallback model with reduced errors after mitigation." Rosa will draft the public message.

oncall-bot: UPDATE: mitigation applied (warmup disabled + routing fallback + node cordoned). Incident now in mitigation state.

Alex (runtime): observed one customer error pattern: heavy concurrent warmup + artifact stream led to combined memory spike -> driver reset. best immediate fix was to avoid warmup at pod init and allow lazy warmup on first request with smaller batch sizes. We'll add a config to disable eager prefill by default for large models as follow-up.

Rosa (Customer Ops): customers notified via email template. will post to status page after 13:05 UTC if no relapse.

Priya (oncall): action items: 1) infra: collect driver/kernel logs and reconcile versions (Mei), 2) runtime: add lazy warmup toggle + safer default for large models (Alex/Liam), 3) ops: customer comms + status page (Rosa). We'll keep this thread updated.

Mei (SRE Lead): starting node investigation now. tagging infra oncall.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: primary symptoms mitigated and customer-impacting errors reduced. Followups assigned for root-cause and postmortem.

Priya (oncall): thanks team. please add any followup notes to the postmortem doc and link PRs to the incident. I'll run the post-incident checklist. :white_check_mark:
